macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rally after Democratic midterm sweep
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 3.03%, the S&P 500 rose 1.58%, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.44% as investors bet that political gridlock could limit policy changes. Technology stocks lagged amid concerns about tighter scrutiny of AI infrastructure spending.[1][2]

items.title: Asian markets mostly higher, but South Korean chips sell off
items.summary: Asian shares generally followed Wall Street higher, while South Korea’s Kospi briefly fell more than 4% as computer-chip stocks faced heavy selling.[2]

items.title: Oil falls to two-month lows
items.summary: Brent crude dropped below $95 per barrel and U.S. crude fell sharply as investors anticipated reduced Middle East escalation risks and a possible resolution to the U.S.-Iran conflict following the election result.[2][3]

items.title: U.S. private-sector hiring exceeds expectations
items.summary: ADP reported that private employers added 86,000 jobs in October, above the roughly 69,000 expected, while the ISM services index came in at 54.5, signaling continued expansion but a modest slowdown.[7]

items.title: Markets price a potential Federal Reserve rate hike
items.summary: Financial markets were assigning nearly an 82% probability to a December Federal Reserve rate hike, according to CME FedWatch data cited in market coverage.[7]

items.title: Eurozone inflation reaches 4%
items.summary: Eurozone inflation rose to 4% in October, twice the European Central Bank’s target, driven largely by higher energy costs and increasing pressure on the central bank’s policy outlook.[3]

items.title: Brazil central bank pauses rate-cutting cycle
items.summary: Brazil’s central bank held its policy rate unchanged after five consecutive cuts as inflation moved further from target and concerns about government spending increased.[3]

items.title: Major companies report earnings amid market rotation
items.summary: Investors were monitoring results from companies including Costco, Arm, McDonald’s, Qualcomm, Uber, McKesson, MercadoLibre, AppLovin, Motorola Solutions, Datadog, and Allstate.[5]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $80,500 as short squeeze drives nearly $800 million in liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed above $80,500, with roughly $794 million in crypto positions liquidated over 24 hours, about 70% of them shorts. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $74.57 million in inflows, ending three consecutive days of outflows.

items.title: Crypto market rallies after Democrats win both chambers of Congress
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $80,484, up 5.7% over 24 hours, while Ether rose 8%, XRP gained 4.7%, and Solana advanced 5.9%. Zcash was among the strongest major-token performers, rising 11.7% ahead of its NU7 network upgrade.

items.title: Democratic congressional victory raises scrutiny of Trump-linked crypto ventures
items.summary: The change in congressional control is expected to bring greater oversight of President Trump’s crypto businesses, including World Liberty Financial, its USD1 stablecoin, and associated tokens. The shift could also affect the outlook for digital-asset legislation and broader sector regulation.

items.title: Polygon community proposes recovery of 70.49 million POL
items.summary: Polygon community members proposed a hard fork to recover 70.49 million POL connected to security incidents involving Polymarket and Binance.

items.title: Riot Platforms reports stronger mining output and major AI data-center lease
items.summary: Riot mined 1,637 Bitcoin in the third quarter, up from 1,406 a year earlier, and reported a surprise profit. The company also announced a 15-year lease covering its Corsicana, Texas, data-center capacity, with approximately $28 billion in contracted revenue over the initial term.

items.title: GAIN token plunges after unauthorized minting vulnerability
items.summary: Griffin AI’s GAIN token reportedly fell as much as 90% after an attacker—or unauthorized party—minted 5 billion tokens shortly after launch, creating severe dilution and selling pressure.

items.title: Zcash rally coincides with upcoming NU7 network upgrade
items.summary: Zcash gained nearly 12% as traders positioned ahead of the NU7 upgrade, which is expected to reduce the target interval between blocks from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Ricursive Intelligence releases Ripple-65B Preview
items.summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, an open-weight general-purpose model derived from the system powering its AI chip-design platform. The company says it achieved a score of 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, which it describes as a U.S. open-weight state-of-the-art result for agentic coding.

items.title: Pangram Labs launches AI-image detection model
items.summary: Pangram Labs unveiled Pangram Image 1.0, a model intended to identify AI-generated images. The company claims 99.2% detection accuracy with a 0.27% false-positive rate.

items.title: Preferred Networks releases PLaMo 3 Translate
items.summary: Preferred Networks released the weights for PLaMo 3 Translate in four sizes ranging from 0.8B to 31B parameters, supporting 53 languages. The company reports particularly strong performance on Japanese-English and multilingual Japanese translation.

items.title: Meta researchers introduce GSLM2 speech model
items.summary: Meta researchers presented GSLM2, a multi-stream speech model designed to learn linguistic structure directly from audio. Reported evaluations across as many as 6 million hours of data and 6.5 billion parameters indicate improved scaling efficiency and stronger linguistic competence.

items.title: TCS study finds limited enterprise autonomy for AI agents
items.summary: A TCS study reported that only about 10% of global enterprises currently allow AI agents to make decisions autonomously. The finding underscores the continuing focus on governance and safeguards as businesses expand agent access to applications and workflows.

items.title: Anthropic reports Claude Opus 5.5 performance and cost gains
items.summary: Anthropic said Claude Opus 5.5 leads in agentic coding and knowledge-work evaluations while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Nintendo launches The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake
items.summary: Nintendo released its remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, using midnight retail openings to mark the debut. The launch arrives ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI, which is scheduled for November 19.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls VI officially titled Sentinel
items.summary: Bethesda and Xbox revealed the official title, The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, alongside a brief teaser. Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier reportedly said the game is more than two years from release.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI anticipation intensifies ahead of launch
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is drawing unusually high consumer and industry attention ahead of its November 19 release, with analysts and observers predicting one of the biggest launches in entertainment history.

items.title: Take-Two again addresses AI use in GTA VI development
items.summary: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick discussed artificial intelligence and the development of Grand Theft Auto VI, while reiterating expectations for an exceptionally large launch.

items.title: GTA VI preorder estimates reportedly surpass $750 million
items.summary: Sensor Tower estimates cited by multiple outlets put Grand Theft Auto VI digital preorders at about 7.71 million units and $751 million in revenue. The figures are unofficial and exclude physical purchases.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: U.S. semiconductor industry expands workforce training
items.summary: Community colleges in Arizona are offering free, three-month semiconductor courses that lead to interviews with major technology companies. The initiative aims to address a looming labor shortage in the U.S. chip industry.

items.title: Cyberattack targets French blood-bank websites
items.summary: French authorities said attackers attempted to manipulate blood-bank systems in a way that could have raised storage temperatures, but the incident was stopped before blood products were damaged.

items.title: Australia’s high court hears challenge to children’s social-media ban
items.summary: Australia’s highest court is hearing legal challenges to a law restricting social-media access for children, with the government arguing that the measure is needed to protect young people’s well-being.

items.title: Canva to cut or restructure 22% of its workforce
items.summary: Australian design-software company Canva is cutting or restructuring 1,271 jobs after growth slowed for the first time in a decade.

items.title: Yellow Card acquires Brazilian virtual-asset provider
items.summary: African stablecoin-payments company Yellow Card acquired Brazil-based virtual-asset service provider GoMoney, marking its entry into the Latin American market.

items.title: Nvidia chips reportedly await approval for shipment to China
items.summary: About 600,000 advanced Nvidia chips are reportedly stored in Hong Kong while Beijing withholds approval for large-scale imports into mainland China.
